title: Keep a pool's minimum below its maximum

blocks.text: A connection pool keeps at least `min` connections open and never more than `max`. Operators change the limits by hand and the autoscaler changes them on its own, from different threads, and every change must also pass the platform's `Policy` (a ceiling per service tier, for example). Last week one service ran with `min` 16 and `max` 12 for an hour: an operator raised the minimum while the autoscaler lowered the maximum, and both changes were accepted. Each limit is an `AtomicInteger` today.

Finish `limits()`, `setMin(...)` and `setMax(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/PoolLimits.java`. You may change how the limits are stored. The policy check calls the config service and can take seconds, and a change must not wait for another change's policy check. When you're done, the limits can never be seen with `min` above `max`, every change that was accepted is in force, and a change that a concurrent change made invalid is refused. About twelve lines in total.
The tests make one change's policy check slow and make another change while it waits.

cases.says: each limit can be changed on its own, and a change is refused when the minimum would exceed the maximum or the policy refuses the pair
a raised minimum and a lowered maximum made at the same time never leave the minimum above the maximum
two changes made at the same time that fit together are both in force afterwards
a change that was valid when it was checked is refused if a change made meanwhile makes it invalid

origin.section: Values That Must Agree Need One Lock or One Immutable Holder Replaced by compareAndSet

concepts: A rule over two variables breaks even when each is atomic; it holds only under one lock or in one immutable holder replaced by compareAndSet with the rule checked on every attempt.
